header.userPrompt: When presenting token summaries, format the big numbers (millions, thousands) appropriately, with separators, so that they are easier to read. Alternatively, maybe we should just print "3.2M" or "103.8K"? Decide which will be better from a UX standpoint

resultJson.description:
The end-of-flow token summary printed by CostTracker renders raw token counts, e.g. `performance: 1000000 in, 0 out ($1.0000*)`. Seven-plus-digit numbers are hard to scan and compare across the by-agent, by-model, and by-role sections. This epic switches the counts to compact human notation ("3.2M", "103.8K") rather than thousands separators ("1,000,000"). Rationale for that UX choice: the summary is read for magnitude comparison, not exact accounting — the precise figure on each line is the dollar cost, which stays untouched; each line can carry up to four counts (in, cached, out, reasoning) plus a cost, so separator-formatted numbers make lines very wide; and compact notation is the established convention in comparable CLI tools (Claude Code itself shows "103.8k tokens").

Format spec: below 1000 print plain digits ("512"); from 1000 use one decimal with a K/M/B suffix ("1.5K", "103.8K", "3.2M"), dropping a trailing ".0" ("2K" not "2.0K"); round half-up and promote units after rounding so 999,950 renders as "1M", never "1000K". B is included because cache-read tokens accumulate across a long flow and can plausibly exceed a billion. Formatting must be locale-independent (no default-locale String.format). The change is fully localized: CostTracker.formatUsage in the flow module is the only place token counts are rendered for users (TerminalEventListener deliberately ignores TokensUsed events, deferring to CostTracker).

tasks.title: Compact token-count formatting in CostTracker summary
tasks.description: In flow/src/main/scala/orca/events/CostTracker.scala, add a private compact-count formatter and apply it to all four counts in formatUsage (inputTokens, cachedInputTokens, outputTokens, reasoningOutputTokens). Spec: n < 1000 → plain digits; n >= 1000 → one decimal + K/M/B suffix with trailing ".0" dropped ("2K", "103.8K", "3.2M"); round half-up; promote the unit after rounding so 999,950 → "1M", not "1000K"; locale-independent string construction (manual/BigDecimal-based, no default-locale String.format). Costs remain exact $X.XXXX — do not touch formatAmount/formatCost. Update the summary method's scaladoc (currently says counts are shown; mention compact notation). In flow/src/test/scala/orca/CostTrackerTest.scala, update the existing expectation "performance: 1000000 in, 0 out ($1.0000*)" to the new "1M in" rendering, keep the "10 in, 5 out" small-number case as-is, and add tests via summary output covering: the 999/1000 boundary, trailing-zero drop (2,000 → "2K"), a decimal case (103,800 → "103.8K"), the M tier, and rounding promotion (999,950 → "1M"). Verify with sbt "flow/testOnly orca.CostTrackerTest" and sbt scalafmtCheckAll.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules and files

- `flow/src/main/scala/orca/events/CostTracker.scala` — the ONLY file whose behavior changes. `CostTracker` is an `OrcaListener` that accumulates `TokensUsed` events by agent/model/role and renders the end-of-run summary. The rendering chain: `summary` (public, returns the full multi-section string) → `formatLine(usage, cost)` → `formatUsage(usage)` (private, currently `s"${usage.inputTokens} in$cached, ${usage.outputTokens} out$reasoning"` with `(N cached)` / `(N reasoning)` parentheticals when non-zero) and `formatCost`/`formatAmount` (dollar figures — leave unchanged). `printSummary()` at the bottom prints it; called from `runner/src/main/scala/orca/flow.scala:220` in a finally block.
- `flow/src/test/scala/orca/CostTrackerTest.scala` — munit `FunSuite` covering the tracker. Directly affected existing tests: "summary formats per-line cost as $X.XXXX with an asterisk on estimates" asserts `out.contains("performance: 1000000 in, 0 out ($1.0000*)")` (must become the compact rendering, e.g. `1M in, 0 out`) and `out.contains("claude: 10 in, 5 out ($0.1000)")` (unchanged — below 1000). Other summary tests assert on labels/sections, not counts, and should pass untouched.

## Key types

- `Usage` (`tools/src/main/scala/orca/events/Usage.scala`): fields `inputTokens: Long` (total prompt tokens, INCLUSIVE of cached), `outputTokens: Long` (inclusive of reasoning), `cost: Option[BigDecimal]`, `cachedInputTokens: Long`, `reasoningOutputTokens: Long`. Counts are `Long` — the formatter must take `Long`.
- `Cost(amount: BigDecimal, estimated: Boolean)` — untouched.

## Scope boundaries (verified)

- `CostTracker.formatUsage` is the single user-facing token-count render site. `TerminalEventListener` (runner module) explicitly no-ops on `TokensUsed` ("Token accounting is owned by CostTracker"). The progress package (`flow/.../progress/`) shows no token counts. Do not go hunting for other sites.
- `orca.util.TextUtil` (tools module) exists as a cross-package text-helper object, but the formatter has exactly one consumer — keep it a private method inside `CostTracker`, matching the existing private `formatAmount`/`modelLabel` helpers there. Do not create a new util.

## Conventions

- MANDATORY: invoke the `direct-style-scala` skill (Skill tool) before touching any Scala code — project CLAUDE.md requires this of subagents too.
- Scala 3 significant-indentation style, `def f(...): T =` with colon-eol bodies; match surrounding code exactly.
- Comment style: scaladoc on non-obvious methods describes usage/contract, never implementation history; inline comments only where non-trivial reasoning is needed (the rounding-promotion edge case qualifies). Keep comments short.
- Tests: munit `FunSuite`, `test("..."):` colon syntax, assertions carry the actual output as the clue argument (`assert(out.contains(...), out)`). Existing tests build events via the local `tokens(agent, model, usage, role)` helper.
- Build/test: `sbt "flow/testOnly orca.CostTrackerTest"` for the suite, `sbt scalafmtAll` to format, `sbt scalafmtCheckAll` to verify formatting (CI fails on it). sbt runs are slow (minutes) — run once after the change is complete, not iteratively.
- Never commit unless explicitly asked.

## Implementation notes

- Half-up rounding with unit promotion is cleanest via `BigDecimal(n).setScale(...)` per-unit then checking whether the rounded mantissa reached 1000 (promote to the next unit), or by rounding first and selecting the unit from the rounded value. `String.format`/`formatted` without an explicit locale is locale-dependent (comma vs period decimal separator) — avoid it; BigDecimal.toString is locale-safe.
- Trailing ".0" drop: after setScale(1), strip a `.0` suffix (or use stripTrailingZeros carefully — beware its scientific-notation output for values like 2E+1; plain string suffix-strip of ".0" is simpler and sufficient since scale is fixed at 1).
